findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed that the heat dish machine is still not repaired, and not reaching a high enough temperatures for sanitizing (165°F). PIC is working with a repair service to get the heat machine back up to a sanitizing temperature of 165°F. Facility is using their triple sinks to sanitize until the heat dish machine is repaired. Inspector will follow up with facility to confirm machine is repaired. Ensure that the temperature of a heat dish machine shall reach 165°F.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.112(A) Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, in a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 90°C (194°F), or less than: (1) For a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 74°C (165°F); or (2) For all other machines, 82°C (180°F). [Pf]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed a container of cream (a TCS product) with a date mark beyond the 7 day rule. CORRECTED: PIC voluntarily discarded the cream, and discussed with Inspector rules for date marking TCS, RTE products. Ensure that any TCS, RTE foods are date marked if they will be in the facility beyond 24 hours of their open or prep date, with the date of prep or open being day 1, and day 7 being the day of final use or discard.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: 2ND REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed there is a significant buildup of dust on the walk-in freezer fans. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the walk-in freezer fans are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed 2 employee bathrooms that are used by women where there was not a lid on the trash receptacles. Inspector discussed with PIC the importance of providing a lidded trash receptacles for bathrooms used by women, including for hygiene purposes and to protect the facility’s plumbing from improperly discarded feminine hygiene products. Ensure that all toilet rooms used by women have a covered trash receptacle.
findings.citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed a wet mop being stored in the lower basin of a mop bucket where it cannot air-dry. Observed 2 wet mops being stored against a wall (which can soil the wall), with one of two mops not being inverted and allowed to air-dry. CORRECTED: PIC relocated both mops to better locations where they can air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies. Ensure mops be stored in positions and locations where they can fully air-dry between uses.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Observed various white powders (ex. sugar, flour, salt) in the kitchen that had been removed from the original packaging and moved into large containers but were not labeled. All easily mistakable foods not in the original container must be labeled with the common name of the food. Ensure that any white powder re-packaged into storage containers are labeled with the common name of the food by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Observed a large container of cream filling stored with the scoop handle directly touching the filling. The PIC was informed and they removed the scoop from the container. They stated that the company policy is that scoops should not be stored within food containers. The PIC will be educating employees about the proper procedure. Ensure that scoop handles for ready-to-eat foods are always stored above food to avoid contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed the cove base underneath the front triple sink is not attached to the wall. The cove base must be sealed to the wall to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure that the cove base is repaired/replaced by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed the facility was preparing donuts during the inspection but there was not a sanitizer bucket available. The PIC was informed and they made a sanitizer bucket during the inspection. Ensure that there is always a sanitizer bucket available during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the walk-in freezer fans are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTIONS DATED 08/23/2022 and 12/14/2023.

Observed a wet wiping cloth sitting on a donut prep counter during the inspection. In-use wet wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizer solution between uses. Wiping cloths can never be stored on counters once wet. The wiping cloth was placed in a sanitizer bucket during the inspection. Ensure that wiping cloths are always stored in chemical solution between uses and laundered daily. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the ice scoop holder by the ice machine was soiled with debris on the bottom. The ice scoop holder and ice scoop were removed from service and cleaned during the inspection. After cleaning the ice scoop holder was free of debris. Ensure that the ice scoop holder is cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed the walk-in freezer fans have an accumulation of dust. The fans must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues. Ensure the fans are cleaned by the next routine inspection. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.
